newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Royale Belge unit to quit reinsurance.
newsitem.headline: Royale Belge unit to quit reinsurance.

text.p: Royale Belge Re, a wholly owned unit of Belgian insurance group Royale Belge, said in a statement on Friday it planned to quit the reinsurance market.
"The board...will propose to its annual shareholders meeting on July 14 to subscribe to no new reinsurance business," the company said in a statement.
The company said its decision followed a review of the worldwide reinsurance market in which it had concluded there was little room for small players.
Royale Belge Re said it had premium income of 6.9 billion Belgian francs ($191 million) in 1996 and made a profit of 386 million francs.

A spokesman for parent Royale Belge was not immediately available to comment on the impact Royale Belge Re's decision would have on its own business, or whether the decision was linked to the strategic review of Royale Belge's business being carried out by its controlling shareholder AXA-UAP of France.
